name: Olivia Teo
life: “I still remember the looping signature I borrowed from my spouse.” On Sunday, near the approach to Seabright Court, Olivia likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I sign my wife's name for deliveries. Tonight I want to learn to write mine on a wage dispute.
appearance: Olivia has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a red windbreaker with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. In conversation Olivia counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Olivia has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To sign a pay query unaided.
family: Gabriel Han is Olivia’s half-sibling. Olivia gets to change the plan. Gabriel offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The misplaced umbrella*, Gabriel says, “I promised never to leave things on the beach.”
connections: Eli Fong. A signed wage query has to make sense in both languages before it travels.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Olivia asks which apartment is expecting someone home and makes sure that household knows about the delay.
